title: Generalized Leibniz-Type Formulas for Mathematical Constants
description: Formalizes the family of Leibniz-type alternating series that converge to mathematical constants, unified through the Dirichlet beta and eta functions

meta.author: Leibniz (1676), Catalan (1865), Dirichlet
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: eta-zeta relation η(s) = (1-2^{1-s})ζ(s). 4 sorries remain for the deepest series identities (alternating harmonic series = ln 2 via Abel summation; β(3) = π³/32 and η(2) = π²/12 via Fourier/zeta values). β(1) = π/4, Catalan-constant convergence/positivity/numeric bounds, and the Leibniz error estimate are now fully proved.
originalContributions: Unified framework: Dirichlet beta (β) and eta (η) functions as Leibniz-type series
Definitions of Catalan's constant G = β(2) and Dirichlet character mod 4
Proved algebraic properties: partial sum recurrences, χ₄ periodicity
Complete table of Leibniz-type formulas: β(1)=π/4, β(2)=G, β(3)=π³/32, η(1)=ln2, η(2)=π²/12
Documented irrationality status of each constant

overview.historicalContext: Leibniz discovered $\pi/4 = 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - \cdots$ in 1676 (though the Kerala school knew equivalent results centuries earlier via Gregory's series). The alternating harmonic series $\ln 2 = 1 - 1/2 + 1/3 - \cdots$ was known to Mercator (1668). Euler systematically evaluated these series in the 1730s-40s, connecting $\beta(3) = \pi^3/32$ to Fourier-type expansions. Dirichlet (1837) revealed the deeper structure: $\beta(s) = L(s, \chi_4)$, a Dirichlet $L$-function for the non-principal character mod 4, whose non-vanishing at $s=1$ proves infinitely many primes $\equiv 1 \pmod{4}$. Catalan introduced $G = \beta(2) \approx 0.9159$ in 1865; its irrationality remains open despite partial results by Zudilin (2001, at least one of $\beta(2)$, $\beta(4)$ is irrational) and Rivoal. The eta-zeta relation $\eta(s) = (1-2^{1-s})\zeta(s)$ was known to Euler and provides the bridge between alternating and non-alternating series.
overview.problemStatement: How do generalized Leibniz-type formulas extend to other constants?
overview.text: The Dirichlet beta and eta functions unify all Leibniz-type alternating series: β(s) = Σ(-1)^n/(2n+1)^s captures π-related constants, while η(s) = Σ(-1)^{n-1}/n^s captures ζ-related constants
overview.proofStrategy: Define the Dirichlet beta and eta functions via partial sums, state convergence results for specific values (s=1,2,3), prove algebraic properties of partial sums, and connect to the underlying L-function structure via the character χ₄.
keyInsights: β(s) captures odd-denominator series (π-related), η(s) captures all-denominator series (ζ-related)
The eta-zeta relation η(s) = (1-2^{1-s})ζ(s) converts between alternating and non-alternating sums
Catalan's constant G = β(2) is perhaps the most important constant whose irrationality is unknown
All these series arise from Dirichlet L-functions: β(s) = L(s,χ₄) for the non-principal character mod 4

All Leibniz-type alternating series arise as evaluations of Dirichlet L-functions: the Leibniz formula gives L(1,χ₄) = π/4 and the alternating harmonic series gives L(1,χ₁) = log 2 via the eta function η(s) = (1-2^{1-s})ζ(s). This L-function perspective unifies seemingly disparate constants through the arithmetic of Dirichlet characters.

sections.title: Overview: The Leibniz-Type Formula Family (β and η)
sections.summary: Module docstring, imports, and namespace/opens. Frames the open question — how the Leibniz series π/4 = Σ(-1)ⁿ/(2n+1) extends to other constants — via the Dirichlet beta function β(s) = Σ(-1)ⁿ/(2n+1)ˢ (odd-denominator, π-related: β(1)=π/4, β(2)=G Catalan, β(3)=π³/32) and the Dirichlet eta function η(s) = Σ(-1)ⁿ⁻¹/nˢ = (1−2¹⁻ˢ)ζ(s) (all-denominator, ζ-related: η(1)=ln2, η(2)=π²/12).
sections.mathContext: The two families are $\beta(s) = \sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n/(2n+1)^s$ (a Dirichlet $L$-function for $\chi_4$) and $\eta(s) = \sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{n-1}/n^s = (1-2^{1-s})\zeta(s)$.

sections.title: PART 1 — The Alternating Harmonic Series (ln 2)
sections.summary: Defines altHarmonicPartialSum n = Σ_{k<n} (-1)ᵏ/(k+1) and states alternating_harmonic_series : the partial sums converge to ln 2. The convergence proof is a `sorry` (line 69) — it needs an Abel/boundary argument on the ln(1+x) Taylor series at x=1, which Mathlib's Real.hasSum_pow_div_log_of_abs_lt only covers for |x|<1.
sections.mathContext: $\eta(1) = \ln 2 = 1 - \tfrac12 + \tfrac13 - \cdots$; the $x=1$ boundary of the $\ln(1+x)$ series needs Abel summation (open sorry).

sections.title: PART 2 — The Dirichlet Beta Function (β(1) = π/4)
sections.summary: Defines dirichletBetaPartialSum s n = Σ_{k<n} (-1)ᵏ/(2k+1)ˢ and proves (no sorry) dirichlet_beta_one : the s=1 partial sums converge to π/4 — after Real.rpow_one collapses (2k+1)^(1:ℝ), the sum is literally Mathlib's Leibniz partial sum, closed by tendsto_sum_pi_div_four.
sections.mathContext: $\beta(1) = \pi/4$ (the original Leibniz series), proved by rewriting to Mathlib's `tendsto_sum_pi_div_four`.

sections.title: PART 3 — Catalan's Constant G = β(2)
sections.summary: Defines catalansConstant = Σ(-1)ⁿ/(2n+1)² and proves (all no sorry) catalan_eq_beta_two (G = β(2) by rfl); the private magnitude-sequence toolkit catG with catG_pos / catG_anti / catG_summable (dominated by the p-series Σ1/(n+1)²) / catG_alt_tsum / catalan_alt_conv; catalan_series_convergent (β partial sums at s=2 → G, via Summable.tendsto_alternating_series_tsum); and catalan_pos (G > 0 from the even partial sum 8/9 as an alternating-series lower bound).

sections.title: PART 4 — β(3) = π³/32
sections.summary: States dirichlet_beta_three : the s=3 beta partial sums converge to π³/32. The proof is a `sorry` (line 189) — a genuinely deep evaluation requiring the Fourier series of x² on [-π,π] or Euler's methods.
sections.mathContext: $\beta(3) = \sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n/(2n+1)^3 = \pi^3/32$ (open sorry; provable via the Fourier expansion of $x^2$).

sections.title: PART 5 — The Dirichlet Eta Function (η(1), η(2))
sections.summary: Defines dirichletEtaPartialSum s n = Σ_{k<n} (-1)ᵏ/(k+1)ˢ and states two convergence results, both `sorry` (lines 208, 218): dirichlet_eta_one (η(1) = ln 2, the same series as PART 1 repackaged) and dirichlet_eta_two (η(2) = π²/12, which would follow from the eta-zeta identity below and ζ(2) = π²/6).
sections.mathContext: $\eta(2) = (1 - 2^{1-2})\zeta(2) = \tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{\pi^2}{6} = \pi^2/12$ (open sorry, depends on the eta-zeta axiom).

sections.title: PART 6 — The Eta-Zeta Relationship (the sole axiom)
sections.summary: The file's single `axiom`, eta_zeta_relation (line 230): η(s) = (1 − 2¹⁻ˢ)ζ(s) for s > 1 — the fundamental identity converting alternating to non-alternating series. This is the one assumption behind the entry's `axiomatized` status; the deep analytic content (interchanging the alternating sum with the zeta sum) is asserted rather than derived.
sections.mathContext: $\eta(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s})\zeta(s)$ for $s>1$; the eta zeros occur where $2^{1-s}=1$. Asserted as an axiom, not proved.

sections.title: PART 7 — The General Leibniz-Type Pattern
sections.summary: A documentation-only table unifying all the formulas as C = Σ(-1)ⁿa(n) for a positive decreasing null sequence a(n): 1/(2n+1)→π/4, 1/(2n+1)²→G, 1/(2n+1)³→π³/32 (the β column, π-related odd denominators); 1/(n+1)→ln2, 1/(n+1)²→π²/12, 1/(n+1)³→3ζ(3)/4 (the η column, ζ-related all denominators).
sections.mathContext: $\beta$ captures odd-denominator ($\pi$-related) series; $\eta$ captures all-denominator ($\zeta$-related) series.

sections.title: PART 8 — Proved Algebraic Relationships and χ₄
sections.summary: Fully-proved (no sorry) structural results: beta_partial_sum_alternating and eta_partial_sum_alternating (the one-term recurrences via Finset.sum_range_succ); then the mod-4 Dirichlet character dirichletCharMod4 (0 on evens, ±1 on n≡1,3 mod 4) with char_mod4_periodic (period 4) and char_mod4_values (χ₄(0..3) = 0,1,0,-1), realizing β(s) = L(s, χ₄).
sections.mathContext: $\chi_4$ is the non-principal character mod 4 with $\beta(s) = L(s,\chi_4)$; periodicity and its four values are proved by `simp`/`decide`.

sections.title: PART 9 — Known and Unknown Irrationality
sections.summary: A documentation table of irrationality/transcendence status: π/4 = β(1) and π³/32 = β(3), ln 2 = η(1) and π²/12 = η(2) are all irrational and transcendental, while Catalan's G = β(2) has UNKNOWN irrationality — one of the most important open constants (Zudilin 2001: at least one of β(2), β(4) is irrational).
sections.mathContext: $G = \beta(2)$ is the notable open case: its irrationality is unknown despite $\beta(1),\beta(3),\eta(1),\eta(2)$ all being transcendental.

sections.title: PART 10 — Numerical Bounds and the Leibniz Error Estimate
sections.summary: Two fully-proved (no sorry) quantitative results. catalan_bounds : 0.91 < G < 0.92, from the alternating-series error bound at 8 terms (|G − S₈| ≤ 1/289 with S₈ ≈ 0.91502). The private leibG toolkit (leibG_nonneg, leibG_anti, leib_alt_conv) then supports leibniz_error_bound : |β_n(1) − π/4| ≤ 1/(2n+1), proved by even/odd case split using Antitone.alternating_series_le_tendsto and tendsto_le_alternating_series — the standard alternating-series estimate reproved by hand because Mathlib's alternating_series_error_bound needs absolute convergence.
sections.mathContext: Alternating-series error control: $|G - S_8| \le 1/289$ gives $0.91<G<0.92$, and $|\beta_n(1) - \pi/4| \le 1/(2n+1)$ quantifies the Leibniz series' slow convergence.

sections.title: PART 11 — Summary
sections.summary: Closing summary docstring tabulating the proved results, the remaining convergence sorries, and the single deep-identity axiom (eta_zeta_relation), plus #check sanity lines and the namespace end. Note: the in-file prose tally is itself partly stale (it lists catalan_bounds and leibniz_error_bound among sorries, though both are now proved); the primary file's live count is 4 sorries + 1 axiom.
sections.mathContext: Live status: 4 open sorries (η(1)/ln2 boundary, β(3), η(1)/η(2) repackaged) and 1 axiom (η = (1−2¹⁻ˢ)ζ); the β/η split unifies all known Leibniz-type series.

crossReferences.description: Answers OQ-02: 'How do generalized Leibniz-type formulas extend to other constants?'
dirichlet_eta_two claims η(2) = π²/12 via η(s) = (1-2^{1-s})ζ(s) at s=2, so the value rests on the Basel-problem evaluation ζ(2) = π²/6 proved in that entry.

Both entries formalize structure around the mod-4 Dirichlet character χ₄; this file identifies β(s) = L(s, χ₄) while Dirichlet's theorem uses the non-vanishing of Dirichlet L-functions at s=1 to prove infinitely many primes in each coprime residue class mod q.

conclusion.summary: Leibniz-type alternating series form a unified family through the Dirichlet beta and eta functions. The beta function captures odd-denominator series (yielding π, Catalan's G, π³/32) while the eta function captures all-denominator series (yielding ln 2, π²/12). The underlying structure is L-functions for Dirichlet characters.
conclusion.implications: The framework reveals that Leibniz's π/4 formula is not isolated but is the first member of an infinite family of series converging to important constants. The irrationality of Catalan's constant G = β(2) remains a major open problem.
openQuestions: Can the irrationality of Catalan's constant be proved or disproved?
Can these series convergence results be proved in Lean using Mathlib's analysis infrastructure?

references.title: Mathematical Constants
references.author: Steven R. Finch
references.venue: Cambridge University Press (Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications 94)
references.description: Catalogues the constants this family produces — Catalan's G = β(2), the Dirichlet beta values β(1) = π/4 and β(3) = π³/32, and the eta values η(1) = ln 2 and η(2) = π²/12 — with their Leibniz-type alternating series and the open irrationality status of G.

references.title: Introduction to Analytic Number Theory
references.author: Tom M. Apostol
references.description: Develops Dirichlet L-functions and the beta/eta functions β(s) = ∑ (−1)ⁿ/(2n+1)^s and η(s) = ∑ (−1)^{n−1}/n^s as L-functions of Dirichlet characters — the unifying structure that places Leibniz's π/4 = β(1) as the first member of the family.

references.title: Pi and the AGM: A Study in Analytic Number Theory and Computational Complexity
references.author: Jonathan M. Borwein and Peter B. Borwein
references.description: Standard reference for series representations of π and related constants, including the alternating (Leibniz–Gregory) series and their acceleration, the analytic backdrop for the Dirichlet-beta family formalized here.
